rows.value: These are group/promoter-level enforcement matters, not findings about any specific Smartworld project SPV. None of the six Smartworld-branded project SPVs tracked in this file (Riverday, Nourish, Suposhaa, Etsy, Adhikaansh, Svabhumi) has been shown to be a named party in these matters.

rows.label: REPORTED STRATEGY
rows.value: Group reportedly acquires standard group-housing land, then stacks Transit-Oriented Development, Transfer of Development Rights, and GRIHA green-building bonuses to multiply buildable Floor Area Ratio beyond what a standard residential license alone would permit.

rows.label: COMMERCIAL TDR INJECTION
rows.value: Reported pattern of injecting commercial TDR into residential-licensed plots (cited example: M3M Capital Phase 2, not one of the six SPVs tracked in this file) to convert standard plots into higher-margin mixed-use development.

rows.label: SCOPE OF THE CLAIM
rows.value: Describes a reported general operating strategy for the group, not a specific transaction on any of the six tracked Smartworld project SPVs. Worth testing directly against each SPV's actual licensed FAR/TDR filings -- not yet done for any of them.

rows.label: GRADE
rows.value: [D] Analytical/reported strategy description -- no specific primary-source filing has been retrieved tying this mechanism to a named Smartworld SPV.

sections.heading: HISTORICAL ORIGIN -- 1980s-1990s LAND ACQUISITION ERA (BACKGROUND CONTEXT)

rows.label: REPORTED PATTERN
rows.value: During the Bansi Lal and Om Prakash Chautala-era Haryana administrations, a commonly reported pattern in Gurugram real estate: the state issues Land Acquisition Act Section 4/6 notifications signaling intent to acquire farmland, private aggregators buy the land cheaply from farmers fearing low state compensation, the state then quietly drops acquisition proceedings, and the aggregator receives a TCP license.

rows.label: SCOPE OF THE CLAIM
rows.value: This describes a general industry pattern reported for Gurugram real estate development broadly during this period, not a specific documented transaction involving M3M/the Bansals or any named parcel. No specific parcel, notification number, or transaction tying this group to this mechanism has been retrieved.

rows.label: GRADE
rows.value: [D] Analytical/background context -- useful as a diligence lens (see MANDATORY DILIGENCE CHECKS below), not as a claim about any specific asset in this file.

rows.label: REPORTED TRANSACTION
rows.value: Dignity Buildcon Pvt Ltd reportedly incorporated in 2007 with approx. Rs. 1 lakh promoter equity, received an unsecured loan of approx. Rs. 22.8 crore from RHC Holdings, used it to acquire land in Sector 66, and by 2009 the entity was sold for approx. Rs. 588.92 crore.

rows.label: RHC HOLDINGS
rows.value: Reported as controlled by the Singh brothers (Ranbaxy/Religare); the Singh brothers were separately subject to fraud investigations in later, unrelated matters (the Fortis/Religare corporate governance matter). Stated as two separate facts -- a lending relationship in 2007, and unrelated later allegations against the lender's principals -- not as evidence that this transaction itself was improper.

rows.label: GRADE
rows.value: [C] Reported public-record claim (share-transfer/company-archive figures), not independently cross-checked here against a primary MCA filing or the actual sale agreement. Specific rupee figures and dates are as supplied; not re-verified.

rows.label: DILIGENCE RELEVANCE
rows.value: If accurate, this is a template for high-leverage, low-promoter-equity SPV structuring. Worth testing whether any of the six currently-tracked Smartworld project SPVs show a similar low-initial-equity, debt-heavy capitalization pattern -- not yet tested against any of them.

sections.heading: MANDATORY DILIGENCE CHECKS -- PROPOSED METHODOLOGY (APPLY PER SPV)

rows.label: 2. INITIAL EQUITY VS. DEBT
rows.value: How much actual promoter equity is in the SPV vs. unsecured loans from related/shadow financiers? Not yet checked for any of the six tracked SPVs.

rows.label: 3. LICENSE EXEMPTION CHECK
rows.value: Was the DTCP license granted under standard protocol, or via an "extreme hardship" or other discretionary exemption under the Haryana Development and Regulation of Urban Areas Act, 1975? Not yet checked for any of the six tracked SPVs.

rows.label: STATUS
rows.value: Proposed framework, not yet applied. This is a methodology note for future diligence work, not a finding.
